title: Training-Free Motion-Bias Calibration for Precipitation Nowcasting: A Negative Result

contributions.purpose: Formalize the motion-bias hypothesis so that post-processing corrections can be rigorously tested.
contributions.mechanism: Defines motion bias via a speed-scale parameter alpha with pre-defined success criteria (|alpha - 1| >= 0.1 indicating correctable bias).
contributions.evaluation: Provides a testable formulation used to evaluate whether EarthFormer's motion is systematically biased.
contributions.source_quote: We formalize motion bias as a testable hypothesis with pre-defined success criteria, enabling rigorous evaluation of post-processing methods.

contributions.purpose: Build and evaluate a training-free motion-bias correction method at scale.
contributions.mechanism: Motion-Bias Calibration (MBC) estimates motion bias via Lucas-Kanade optical flow and corrects predictions through learned cumulative-translation warping, with Huber, OLS, and gated fitting variants.
contributions.evaluation: Evaluated on 12,159 SEVIR test samples; all MBC variants degrade CSI by 0.0014-0.0018 relative to the raw baseline.
contributions.source_quote: We implement MBC with multiple fitting variants (Huber, OLS, gated) and evaluate on 12,159 SEVIR test samples.

contributions.purpose: Distinguish genuine motion correction from mere interpolation artifacts.
contributions.mechanism: Designs a random-direction warp control that applies warping in a direction unrelated to estimated motion.
contributions.evaluation: The control confirms that observed CSI changes are interpolation artifacts rather than motion-specific correction.
contributions.source_quote: We design a random-direction warp control that isolates interpolation artifacts from motion-specific correction.

contributions.purpose: Report the empirical verdict on the motion-bias hypothesis for this model-dataset pair.
contributions.mechanism: Measures the fitted speed-scale parameter and compares MBC-corrected CSI against the raw baseline.
contributions.evaluation: Negative result: alpha = 0.921 (within 8% of neutral, |alpha - 1| < 0.1) indicates no systematic motion bias, and all MBC variants degrade CSI; the gap to cascaded methods (CasCast CSI-219 = 0.2841 vs EarthFormer 0.2078) needs fundamentally different approaches.
contributions.source_quote: We report a negative result: EarthFormer does not exhibit systematic motion bias on SEVIR, and the performance gap to cascaded methods requires fundamentally different approaches.

notes: Negative-result paper (stated in title and abstract): the hypothesis that deterministic nowcasters exhibit correctable motion bias is refuted for EarthFormer/SEVIR; all MBC variants degrade CSI by 0.0014-0.0018 vs raw baseline. Pages 1-2 contain Introduction and Method only (no Related Work section), so no explicit extend/adapt/replace positioning statement was present.
